images.title: Different shape, same sixth
images.purpose: Show that a square piece and a triangle piece can both be 1/6 of the chikki, because each covers 4 of the 24 small squares.
images.composition: Two equal chikki grids side by side with wide space between them, and one short line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Two chikkis of exactly the same size, each a grid of 24 equal small squares, 6 across and 4 down. Left: thick lines cut it into 6 square pieces of 2 by 2; one square piece filled teal #0072B2. Right: thick lines cut it into 3 upright strips of 2 across and 4 down, each strip cut corner to corner into 2 equal triangles; one triangle filled amber #E69F00. Exactly 2 grids, 6 pieces in each, 2 coloured pieces.

images.takeaway: Equal coverage, not shape, sets the fraction.
images.description: Two same-size 6 by 4 chikki grids: one cut into 6 squares of 2 by 2, one cut into 6 triangles; a teal square and an amber triangle each cover 4 small squares and are each 1/6.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the small squares each coloured piece covers and say why both are one sixth.

image_decisions.why: Two same-size chikkis cut two ways show that pieces of different shape can be the same fraction.
